copy.error_addition_too_low: It looks like you did not add all the parts, or you missed a number along the way.
copy.error_addition_too_high: It looks like you added something twice or made a mistake in a middle sum.
copy.error_addition_default: It helps to check the addition step by step - you can break into tens and ones and add part by part.
copy.error_subtraction: In subtraction it is easy to mix up the order of the numbers. Check that you reduced the larger number, not the other way around.
copy.error_multiplication: In multiplication people sometimes mix multiply and add. Make sure you repeated the correct number the correct number of times.
copy.error_division: In division, check that the result times the divisor returns the original number.
copy.error_fractions: With fractions people often forget a common denominator or change the denominator instead of only the numerator.
copy.error_percentages: With percents a common mistake is confusing a part of 100 with ordinary add/subtract. Try writing the fraction first (for example {example}).
copy.error_sequences: In sequences many people miss the constant difference. Check again what happens between two neighboring terms.
copy.error_decimals: With decimals mistakes happen when you do not line up the points or forget how many digits are after the decimal.
copy.error_rounding: When rounding it is easy to mix up the next digit. Check whether it is {low} (round down) or {high} (round up).
copy.error_equations: In missing-number equations many people guess. Use the inverse operation and bring both sides back to the same number.
copy.error_compare: When comparing numbers the common mistake is mixing up which is larger, especially with decimals. Try comparing the whole-number parts first.
copy.error_number_sense: Check the place-value breakdown (tens/hundreds/ones) again, or whether the number is even/odd. These are easy to mix up when rushing.
copy.error_factors_multiples: With factors and multiples it is easy to mix up "what divides the number" and "what you get when multiplying". Try listing all factors or multiples on the side.
copy.error_word_problems: In word problems the common mistake is choosing the wrong operation (add instead of subtract, etc.). Try writing a simple exercise that matches the story.
copy.hint_addition_add_three: Add two numbers, then add the third: {expr}.
copy.hint_addition_complement: Find how much is needed to reach ten / a round number – you do not need the full long addition.
copy.hint_addition_missing: If you have __ + b = c, the missing number is {missing_first}. If you have a + __ = c, the missing number is {missing_second}.
copy.hint_addition_default: Use the "column" method or hops on a number line: addition = putting amounts together.
copy.hint_subtraction_missing: If you have __ - b = c, the missing number is {missing_first}. If you have a - __ = c, the missing number is {missing_second}.
copy.hint_subtraction_default: Check which number is larger. Subtraction = how much is needed from the smaller to the larger, or how much you take away from the larger.
copy.hint_multiplication: Think of multiplication as repeated addition: {product} means adding {a} to itself {b} times.
copy.hint_division: Division = how many times the smaller number fits into the larger, or how many are in each group when sharing equally.
copy.hint_fractions_same_den: When denominators are the same – keep the denominator and work only with the numerators.
copy.hint_fractions_default: When denominators differ – find a common denominator, rewrite the fractions, then add or subtract.
copy.hint_percentages: Percents are parts of {hundred}. {ten} is one tenth, {twenty_five} is one fourth, {fifty} is one half. Try rewriting as a simple part.
copy.hint_sequences: Check what happens between each pair of neighboring numbers – what is added or subtracted each step.
copy.hint_decimals: Line up the decimal points and compute as if they were whole numbers, then put the decimal point back in the right place.
copy.hint_rounding: Find the place you are rounding to (tens/hundreds) and look at the next digit: {low} round down, {high} round up.
copy.hint_equations: For equations with a missing number, use the inverse operation: addition uses subtraction, multiplication uses division, and so on.
copy.hint_compare: Picture the numbers on a number line: farther right means larger. For decimals, compare the whole-number parts first.
copy.hint_number_sense_place: Break the number into tens/hundreds/ones: for example {example} is {tens} tens and {ones} ones.
copy.hint_number_sense_neighbors: One before – subtract {one}. One after – add {one}.
copy.hint_number_sense_complement: Find how much is needed to complete ten/one hundred – that is the difference between the two numbers.
copy.hint_number_sense_even_odd: Look at the ones digit: {even} – even. {odd} – odd.
copy.hint_number_sense_default: Think about number sense – tens, ones, neighbors, even/odd.
copy.hint_factors_multiples: A factor divides a number with no remainder. A multiple is what you get when you multiply the number by a whole number.
copy.hint_word_problems: Read slowly, mark the numbers, and turn the story into a simple exercise (add, subtract, multiply, or divide).
copy.hint_ratio: Find what to multiply both parts of the ratio by to match the numbers in the question.
copy.hint_scale: A scale of 1:X means every cm on the map = X cm in real life. Multiply or divide accordingly.
copy.hint_divisibility: Try dividing the number by the divisor and check whether you get a whole number (no remainder).
copy.hint_powers: A power = repeated multiplication of the base by itself. For example: 3² = 3 × 3 = 9, 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
copy.hint_order_of_operations: Remember order of operations: parentheses first, multiply/divide before add/subtract.
copy.hint_estimation: Round each number to the nearest tens/hundreds, then compute an estimate.
copy.hint_zero_one_properties: A number × 0 = 0. A number × 1 = the same number. A number + 0 = the same number.
copy.hint_division_with_remainder: Find how many times the divisor fits in – and what is left. Check: divisor × quotient + remainder = dividend.
copy.hint_default: Try solving the question using the matching topic.
copy.age_g12_addition: 💡 Try thinking of it this way: you have {a} circles, and you add {b} more circles. How many circles do you have now? Try counting: {count_up} up to {answer}!
copy.age_g12_subtraction: 💡 Try thinking of it this way: you have {a} circles, and you take away {b} circles. How many circles are left? Try counting backward: {count_down} up to {answer}!
copy.age_g12_multiplication: 💡 Multiplication is like repeated addition! {expr} is like {repeated}... ({b} times). Try counting: {count_mult} up to {answer}!
copy.age_g12_division: 💡 Division is like sharing into groups! {expr} is like taking {a} circles and sharing them into {b} equal groups. How many circles in each group? {answer}!
copy.age_g12_default: 💡 Try thinking about the exercise in a simple way. The correct answer is {answer}.
copy.age_g34_addition_break: 💡 Try thinking about addition: {sum_eq}. If it is hard, try breaking it apart: {break_eq}
copy.age_g34_subtraction_break: 💡 Try thinking about subtraction: {diff_eq}. If it is hard, try breaking it apart: {break_eq}
copy.age_g34_step_default: 💡 Try thinking about the exercise step by step. The correct answer is {answer}.
